question: What is your main job as a health worker when an unexpected pregnancy emergency happens in the community?

options.A: Provide first-line stabilization and arrange quick transport
options.B: Wait for the patient to reach a specialist hospital
options.D: Perform immediate major surgery in the village

explanation: You've got this! Since village clinics don't have operating theatres, your primary duty is to stabilize the mother and get her safely to a higher center. Great job keeping her safe! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h1)

question: What does the 'three delays model' help nurses and midwives understand?

options.A: How long a normal labor stage is allowed to last
options.B: Why mothers experience severe delays in accessing life-saving care
options.C: When to administer routine antenatal vitamins
options.D: The exact timing of placental separation after delivery

explanation: Spot on! The three delays model looks at the barriers in seeking care, reaching a facility, and receiving treatment that contribute to maternal deaths. Every step counts! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h1)

question: Which symptom during the final months of pregnancy strongly points to placenta previa?

options.A: High fever with foul-smelling amniotic fluid
options.B: Sudden swelling of the feet only
options.D: Severe painful contractions with a rigid belly

explanation: Well done! Placenta previa happens when the placenta covers the cervix, which typically causes sudden, painless, bright red bleeding. You are mastering your obstetric signs! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h2)

question: A pregnant woman in your community presents with a rigid, painful tummy and dark bleeding. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: You nailed it! When the placenta separates early, blood gets trapped behind it, causing a painful, hard uterus and dark bleeding. Keep up the brilliant thinking! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h2)

question: Why do we frequently place a pregnant woman in shock on her left side?

options.A: To make it easier to perform a cesarean section locally
options.B: To stop excessive postpartum bleeding instantly
options.C: To speed up the delivery of the placenta
options.D: To prevent the heavy uterus from pressing on major blood vessels

explanation: Brilliant! Lying on the left side takes the heavy weight off the inferior vena cava, helping blood flow smoothly back to the heart. Simple trick, life-saving result! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h3)

question: You are reviving a woman with severe shock from bleeding. What size of IV cannula should you secure first?
explanation: You got it! Large-bore cannulas let fluids and blood flow in rapidly when treating severe shock. In an emergency, bigger is definitely better! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h3)

question: What is the most common cause of heavy bleeding right after childbirth (primary PPH)?
explanation: Spot on! Uterine atony happens when the uterine muscles are too tired to clamp down after delivery. Recognizing this helps you save mothers every day! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h4)

question: Why does a full bladder often make postpartum bleeding worse?

options.A: It blocks the release of oxytocin from the brain
options.B: It causes severe high blood pressure in the mother
options.C: It pushes the uterus upward and stops it from contracting
options.D: It dilutes the clotting factors in the bloodstream

explanation: Fantastic! A full bladder pushes the uterus out of place so the muscles can't squeeze tightly around those open blood vessels. Always remember to check the bladder! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h4)

question: What is the go-to medication for stopping and preventing seizures in severe preeclampsia?
explanation: You're doing great! Magnesium sulfate is the gold standard for managing eclamptic seizures and keeping mothers safe. A true midwifery essential! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h5)

question: Before giving another dose of magnesium sulfate, which clinical sign must you check first?

options.B: Size of the liver and spleen

explanation: Awesome job! Losing the knee-jerk reflex is an early warning sign that magnesium is building up too much in the body, well before breathing slows down. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which sign warns you that the uterus might soon rupture during prolonged, difficult labor?

options.A: Formation of a Bandl's retraction ring on the abdomen

explanation: You've got this! A visible retraction ring means the top part of the uterus is thickening while the bottom stretches dangerously thin. Such a crucial clinical catch! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the safest step for a woman experiencing true obstructed labor in a remote village?

options.A: Perform manual pelvic widening in the community clinic
options.B: Encourage aggressive pushing in a squatting position
options.C: Administer oxytocin drip to speed up contractions
options.D: Arrange immediate emergency transfer for surgical delivery

explanation: Spot on! Obstructed labor means the baby cannot pass naturally, so emergency surgery is the only safe answer. Never give oxytocin here—it causes rupture! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is a key part of a safe emergency obstetric referral from a community clinic?

options.A: Ensuring a trained health worker accompanies the patient
options.B: Sending the patient alone with a family member only
options.C: Withholding all intravenous fluids during transit
options.D: Waiting until daylight before arranging any travel

explanation: Brilliant! Having a trained provider ride along means vital signs are watched and complications like bleeding or seizures can be managed on the way. Teamwork saves lives! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h7)

question: Why is proper clinical notes sent along with an emergency referral so important?

options.A: It acts as a formal receipt for community transport payment
options.B: It prevents the receiving hospital from asking any questions
options.C: It provides essential clinical history to speed up hospital treatment
options.D: It gives the referral team legal protection against lawsuits

explanation: You nailed it! Sharing past findings, treatments given, and vitals helps the hospital team jump right into action without wasting precious time repeating tests. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h7)

question: What is a major part of making an individual birth preparedness plan with a pregnant woman?

options.A: Identifying emergency transport and travel funds
options.B: Booking a private room at a tertiary hospital
options.C: Planning an elective induction at 37 weeks
options.D: Purchasing expensive formula milk in advance

explanation: Well done! Planning ahead for transport and money cuts out dangerous delays when sudden emergencies pop up. You're thinking like a true public health nurse! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h8)

question: Why is it important to involve traditional leaders and birth attendants in community maternal health programs?

options.A: They provide financial loans to build local maternity clinics
options.B: They can legally perform emergency surgeries in villages
options.C: They help encourage early reporting of danger signs and prompt referral
options.D: They replace the need for professional midwives entirely

explanation: Spot on! Partnering with community influencers bridges traditional practices with modern healthcare, making sure mothers get to the clinic on time. Excellent perspective! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h8)
